whyThisMatters: If you can name the trick out loud together, you will spot it faster on your own — whether it shows up in a rotation link, a phone call, or a fund request, even with limited time online. Today's riddles use the same patterns Offshore Crew sees every day.
rememberThis: This month gave these tricks a name — keep using them. STOP before you tap a link or hand over anything, VERIFY through a channel you already trust, then REPORT.

discussionPrompts: Ask which two terms are easiest to mix up — VISHING and GIFT-CARD SCAM often happen in the same call, but the ask is different.
Ask for a real example from their own phone or inbox that matches one of these terms.
Ask someone to explain UNKNOWN USB STICK in their own words, without using the term itself.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: People most often mix up VISHING and GIFT-CARD SCAM. Both can arrive as an urgent phone request, so people pick one when the riddle points to the other. The difference: vishing is about a caller trying to get your password or a code; a gift-card scam is about a caller trying to get you to spend money and hand over the codes.

riddles.riddle: In your rotation email the blue text shows the real crew-portal address, but pressing and holding it sends you somewhere with an extra word in the name. What trick am I?
I am a small device with no label, taped to a shared bridge computer. Plugging me in to check whose I am is exactly what I'm hoping for. What trick am I?
I call the ship's phone claiming to be IT support, and ask you to say your password and a code out loud right now. What trick am I (a voice-call phishing attempt)?
I am an urgent message from your "vessel manager" asking you to buy gift cards for a port due and send me the codes. What trick am I?
I give you only 2 hours to sign your Seafarer Employment Agreement renewal or I say you'll lose your sign-on date. What trick am I?
I am the three-step habit: 1. STOP before you act, 2. VERIFY using a number or portal you already trust, 3. REPORT to the IT Service Desk. What is this rule called?
